question.prompt: Let \(S\) be the set \(\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 19\}.\) For \(a,\) \(b \in S,\) define \(a \succ b\) to mean that either \(0 \lt a - b \le 9\) or \(b - a \gt 9.\) How many ordered triples \((x, y, z)\) of elements of \(S\) have the property that \(x \succ y,\) \(y \succ z,\) and \(z \succ x?\)

solutions.explanation:
For two distinct labels, exactly one precedes the other under \(\succ\), and no label precedes itself. Thus every eligible triple has three distinct entries. Also, each label \(a\) precedes exactly nine labels: count backward nine places from \(a\), wrapping from \(1\) to \(19\). This describes exactly the two alternatives in the definition.

It is easier first to count unordered triples. Such a triple either forms a cycle or has a label that precedes both others. To justify this classification, suppose no label precedes both others and choose labels with \(u\succ v\). The third label \(w\) must satisfy \(w\succ u\), since otherwise \(u\) precedes both. Then \(v\succ w\), since otherwise \(w\) precedes both. These three relations form a cycle. Moreover, two labels cannot each precede both others, because that would require both directions for their pair.

There are \(\binom{19}{3}=969\) unordered triples altogether. To obtain a triple that is not a cycle, choose its unique label that precedes both others, then choose two of the nine labels it precedes. This counts every such triple exactly once, giving
\[
19\binom{9}{2}=19\cdot36=684.
\]
Therefore there are \(969-684=285\) unordered cyclic triples. Each has exactly three eligible ordered listings: choose the first entry, after which the direction of the cycle forces the other two. Hence the requested number is
\[
3\cdot285=\boxed{855},
\]
choice \(\text{B}\).
solutions.title: Count the triples that are not cycles

solutions.explanation:
First count unordered triples by writing their distinct labels as \(a<b<c\). Define the positive gaps
\[
p=b-a,\qquad q=c-b.
\]
One cyclic direction is \(b\succ a\), \(c\succ b\), and \(a\succ c\). By the definition, this occurs exactly when
\[
p\le9,\qquad q\le9,\qquad p+q>9.
\]
The reverse cyclic direction would require both \(p>9\) and \(q>9\), which is impossible because \(p+q=c-a\le18\). Thus the displayed conditions describe every cyclic triple.

Group the triples by their span \(d=c-a=p+q\), where \(10\le d\le18\). For a fixed \(d\), the allowed values of \(p\) are
\[
d-9,d-8,\ldots,9,
\]
so there are \(19-d\) gap pairs. Independently, the smallest label \(a\) can be any of \(1,2,\ldots,19-d\). The span, smallest label, and first gap determine the triple uniquely, so the number of unordered cyclic triples is
\[
\sum_{d=10}^{18}(19-d)^2
=9^2+8^2+\cdots+1^2
=285.
\]
For each cyclic triple, any of its three labels can be the first entry, and the other two entries are then forced by the cycle. Consequently the number of ordered triples is \(3\cdot285=\boxed{855}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
